pages.title: Start a release
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release editors (NRMS.Editor).

## Create the release

1. In **Releases**, choose **New release**.
2. Choose the **Type**: **Release**, **Story**, **Factsheet** or **Advisory**.
3. Choose the **Page title**, such as **News Release** or **Backgrounder**. Choosing one also sets the usual **Layout** and **Page image** for it; you can change them.
4. Choose the **Layout**: **Formal** or **Informal**.
5. Choose a **Page image**, or **(none)**. Advisories have none.
6. Enter the **Headline**.
7. If the release is for a Calendar activity, enter its number in **Activity ID**. See below.
8. Enter the **Location**, such as VICTORIA.
9. Tick the **Ministries**. If you tick more than one, choose the **Lead ministry**.
10. Tick the **Sectors**, **Themes** and **Tags** that fit. Advisories have none.
11. Tick any **Media distribution lists** the release should go to. An advisory must have at least one before it can be published.
12. Choose **Create release**.

The release opens, ready to write. It is a **Draft** in the **Drafts** folder. Nobody is emailed and nothing is public.

If something is missing, a box headed "Fix these to create" lists it, such as "Choose a page title." or "Enter a headline.". Each line links to its field.

If the **Page title** list is empty, the page says "No page titles are set up yet. An administrator adds them under Release page titles." Ask a Core administrator.

## Which type to choose

| Type | Ministries | Sectors, themes, tags | Media lists | News On Demand subscribers | Can be unpublished |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Release** | At least one | At least one sector | Allowed | Emailed unless you untick it | Yes |
| **Story** | At least one | At least one sector | No | Not emailed unless you tick it | Yes |
| **Factsheet** | At least one | At least one sector | Allowed | Not emailed unless you tick it | Yes |
| **Advisory** | Optional | None | At least one | Never | No: once sent, it stays sent |

## Start from a Calendar activity

If you have Calendar access, a release can be linked to a Calendar activity.

- On **Forecast**, choose **Start a release** under the activity. **New release** opens with the activity filled in.
- Or type the number in **Activity ID**. The activity's title, ministry and start appear under the field, and its "Translations required", if any.
- Choose **Fill in from activity 3** (the button names the number) to copy its start (as the planned publish date), its city (as the location), its lead and shared ministries, sectors, themes and tags. Check them before you create the release.

Nothing is filled in for an activity that has ended, or whose category doesn't start with "Approved"; the page says which. Other things you may see under the field:

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| "Calendar activity 3: its details aren't shown to you." | It is confidential, or your Calendar access doesn't let you see it. |
| "Calendar activity 3 has been deleted." | It can't be linked. |
| "No Calendar activity has ID 3." | Check the number. |
| "Legacy activity 3, not migrated" | A release brought over from the old system names an activity that didn't come across. It keeps that number until you change it. |

You can link or change the activity later in **Publish settings** on the release, as **Calendar activity ID**. Once a release is linked, the activity shows its status in the Calendar within a minute of each change.

pages.title: Write a release
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release editors (NRMS.Editor).

At the top of a release you see its type, status, reference number and headline. Below that, under "Before this can be approved:" and "Before this can be published:", is what is still missing.

On a wide screen, the release is on the left, and **Actions**, **Publish settings** and **Release info** are on the right. On a narrow screen they come one after another.

## Save your changes

You can change several parts of the release, then save them all at once.

1. Make your changes. Each part you changed says **Unsaved** beside its heading.
2. A bar along the bottom lists them: "You have unsaved changes in: …".
3. Choose **Save changes** in that bar, or press Ctrl+S (Command+S on a Mac). Pressing Enter in a one-line field saves too.
4. The bar says "All changes saved." for a moment, then goes.

If one part can't be saved, the bar says "Couldn't save page details. See why in that section." Choose the link to go to the message. Parts after it are not saved yet and keep your changes.

While anything is unsaved, **Approve**, **Publish now** and **Schedule** are greyed out, with "Save your changes to … first." under them.

If you try to leave with unsaved changes, a box asks "Leave anyway and discard them?" Choose **Stay** to go back, or **Leave** to lose them. If your sign-in runs out while you are writing, sign in again in the same browser tab: the text you typed in a document comes back.

"Someone else changed this — reload to see their changes." means another person saved this release after you opened it. Choose **Reload**. Copy anything you typed first, because reloading shows their version.

**If the release is already published, saving any change republishes it at once.** See [Correct, feature, unpublish or delete](manual:editor-correct-unpublish-delete).

## Documents

A release has one or more documents, such as the news release and a backgrounder. Each has an **English** tab, and a **French** tab once you add one.

Each document has a **Page title**, **Organizations**, **Headline**, **Subheadline**, **Byline**, **Body** and **Contacts**. With the **Formal** layout, **Organizations** must be filled in before you can publish.

The **Body** toolbar has **Bold**, **Italic**, **Bulleted list**, **Numbered list**, **Link** and **Insert asset**. Pasted text keeps only that formatting.

To show a video or photo inside the body:

1. Put the cursor where it should go.
2. Choose **Insert asset**.
3. Paste a YouTube, Flickr or SoundCloud link and choose **OK**.

Up to 10 links in one body show as media. Others show as plain links, and so does a Flickr photo that isn't public when you save.

To add a contact, choose **Add contact** and type it in **Contact 1**. The first line is its title. A document can have up to 20.

To work with documents:

- **Add document**: enter its **Page title**, choose its **Layout**, then choose **Add**.
- **Move up** or **Move down**, or drag the handle, to change the order.
- **Remove**, then **Confirm remove**, deletes the document and its French text. This can't be undone. A release always keeps one document.

## French text

1. Choose **Add French translation** on the document.
2. Choose the **French** tab and fill it in. Once the French tab exists, its headline, body and organizations must be filled in before you can publish.
3. To take it away, choose **Remove French translation**, then **Confirm remove**. This can't be undone.

A French PDF goes under **Files** instead. See [Photos, video and files](manual:editor-files-and-media).

## Page details

- **URL key**: the last part of the release's public address. A release or advisory gets one when it is approved. A story's or factsheet's comes from its headline, and you can change it until it is scheduled.
- **Redirect URL**: fill this in only to send visitors to another page instead.
- **Location**: the place at the start of the release, up to 50 characters.
- **Summary**: what subscribers see in their email. It fills itself from the start of the body, and **Documents** shows "(auto)" until you change it.
- **Social media summary** and **Keywords**.

Advisories have no summary, social media summary or keywords.

## Categories

**Categories** shows what is ticked. Choose **Edit categories** to change the **Ministries**, **Lead ministry**, **Sectors**, **Themes** and **Tags**.

These decide which subscribers are emailed and which public pages list the release. You need at least one ministry and one sector to publish, and a lead ministry when you tick more than one.

## Similar published releases

Use it to check whether something like this has gone out before.

1. Save first: it compares the release as last saved.
2. Choose **Open similar-release search**, then **Find similar**.
3. You see up to 10 published releases, each with its date, lead ministry, **AI match** or **Text match**, and a link that opens the public page in a new tab.

Nothing is sent until you choose **Find similar**. Where the site uses AI matching, the panel says "Sends this draft's text to the AI service to compare." If that service isn't available, you get text matches and the panel says so.

## Release info

- **Key** and **Reference (NEWS number)**, or "(none yet)".
- **View on site** opens the public page. It works only while the release is published.
- **View PDF** opens the release as a PDF.
- **Email me a copy** emails the release to you. You see "Sent to" and your address.
- **History** lists what was done and by whom. Tick **Show all** to include every edit. **Published copies** lists each time it went out.

pages.title: Photos, video and files
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release editors (NRMS.Editor).

Advisories have no media asset, translations or media files.

## The main photo or video

**Media asset** holds the one photo or video shown with the release.

1. Paste a YouTube or Flickr link, or https://news.gov.bc.ca/live, into **Asset URL**.
2. Enter **Alt text**: a short description of the photo or video for people who can't see it, up to 149 characters.
3. Choose **Save changes**.

Under the heading you then see what it is: "YouTube video.", "Live broadcast embed." or, for a Flickr photo, one of these:

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| "Public on Flickr." | Ready. |
| "Private — will be made public when the release publishes." | Leave it. Publishing makes it public. |
| "This photo no longer exists on Flickr." | Check the link, or choose another photo. |
| "Flickr can't be reached right now." | Try again later. You can still publish; see below. |

Links that are refused when you save:

| Message | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Facebook is no longer supported due to privacy concerns. Use YouTube or Flickr URLs instead." | Use a YouTube or Flickr link. |
| "Use a YouTube or Flickr URL, or https://news.gov.bc.ca/live." | Other sites can't be used. |
| "That Flickr link doesn't point to a photo." | Use the link to one photo, not an album or profile. |

## If Flickr is down when the release publishes

- At the publish time, the Hub tries to make the photo public for up to 2 minutes.
- If it can't, it goes out up to 2 minutes late, without the photo. The release and its row in the folders show a **Flickr alert**, and an alert email goes to the people set up to receive Flickr alerts.
- The Hub keeps trying for 24 hours. When the photo becomes public, the release republishes with it by itself. Nobody is emailed again.
- If it still fails after 24 hours, the alert says "The release is live without it — re-add or replace the photo." Change the **Asset URL** and save.

## Translations and media files

**Files** holds files people can open from the public release. On an advisory it says "An Advisory has no translations or media files." and offers no upload.

- **Translations**: PDFs, such as the release in French or another language. Choose **Upload a translation (PDF)** and pick the file.
- **Media files**: PDF, PNG or JPEG files, such as a photo or a fact sheet. Choose **Upload a media file** and pick the file. **Includes additional media assets** in **Media asset** is ticked for you.

Each file can be up to 25 MB. A larger file isn't uploaded. A file is saved as soon as it is uploaded; you don't need **Save changes**. Choose a file's name to open it.

Files can be opened by the public only while the release is published. Before then, and after an unpublish, only Hub staff can open them.

To remove a file, choose **Remove** and its name, then **Confirm remove**. This can't be undone.

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| "This file isn't a PDF." | Translations must be PDFs. |
| "Upload a PDF, PNG or JPEG file." | Media files must be one of those. |
| "The file is empty." | Pick the file again. |
| "photo.jpg is too large to upload. A file can be at most 25 MB." | The file is over 25 MB. Make it smaller. |
| "A file can be at most 25 MB." | The same, found while uploading. |

Uploading or removing a file on a published release republishes it at once, as a correction.

pages.title: Approve, publish and schedule
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release editors (NRMS.Editor).

A release goes from **Draft** to **Approved**, then out now or at a set time. **Actions** shows only the buttons that fit the release's status. Each step acts on the release as saved, so save your changes first.

When a button is greyed out, the reasons are listed under it, such as "Approve is unavailable until:" and "Choose at least one ministry.". Each reason links to the part of the release to fix.

## Approve

1. Choose **Approve**. A box asks "Approve this release?"
2. If the release still has placeholder text, such as "TBD", "TBC", "to come", "XX" or "[insert", the box lists where. Fix it, or choose **Approve anyway** if it is meant to be there.
3. Choose **Approve**.

The release gets a reference number, such as NEWS-00010. A release or advisory also gets its release number, such as 2026HLTH0003-000008, which becomes its public address. **Publish now** and **Schedule** appear. Nobody is emailed.

To approve, a release needs at least one ministry, and a lead ministry when it has more than one. "This ministry is no longer active. Change the lead ministry to its successor before approving." means the lead ministry was replaced; choose the new one in **Categories**.

## Publish now

1. Choose **Publish now**. A box asks "Publish this release now?" and lists what will happen:
   - where it is published, such as "Publishes to news.gov.bc.ca now.";
   - which media distribution lists it is sent to, or "No media distribution lists.";
   - which News On Demand subscribers are emailed, such as "Emails News on Demand subscribers who follow any of: Health — and everyone subscribed to all news.", or "News on Demand subscribers will not be emailed."
2. Check the list. Choose **Publish now**.

The status shows **Publishing...**, then **Published**, usually within a minute. The page updates by itself: "This page updates on its own until the release is done — no need to reload."

## Schedule

1. Choose **Schedule**. If the release has a planned publish date still ahead, the date and time are filled in from it.
2. Enter the **Date** and **Time (BC time)**. A time that has passed shows "Choose a time in the future, or use Publish now."
3. Choose **Confirm schedule**. A box asks, for example, "Schedule this release for Friday, November 20, 2026 at 10:00 AM Pacific time?" and lists who will be emailed, as for **Publish now**.
4. Choose **Schedule**.

The release moves to **Scheduled**. At that time it publishes by itself and the emails go out. Until then nothing is public: not the page, not its files, not the emails.

You can still change a scheduled release. What goes out is the release as saved at the publish time.

## The planned publish date

**Planned publish date (not yet committed)**, in **Publish settings**, is only a plan: nothing happens at that time. It shows on **Forecast** and makes the status **Planned**. Choose **Clear planned date** to remove it. Only **Schedule** commits a time.

## Who is emailed

Set this in **Publish settings** before you publish.

- **Send to News On Demand subscribers**: ticked for releases, unticked for stories and factsheets, and not available for advisories.
- **Send to media distribution lists**: tick it, then tick the lists. A retired list a release already had shows "(retired)" and gets nothing.

See [Who is emailed, and when it goes public](manual:editor-what-happens-next).

## Take back an approval or a schedule

- **Cancel schedule** stops a scheduled release from going out. It goes back to **Drafts** as approved, and its time stays as the planned date. It doesn't ask first.
- **Return to draft** makes an approved or scheduled release a draft again. A box asks "Return this release to draft?" and says it gives up its reference number and release number; it gets new ones when it is approved again. Choose **Return to draft**. This is only for a release that has never been published.

## If publishing fails

The status shows **Failed** and the release goes back to **Drafts**. A red box headed "This release failed" says why. Fix it, save, and choose **Publish now** or **Schedule** again.

Other refusals you may see:

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| "Set a URL key in Page details before this can be published." | A story or factsheet needs a URL key. |
| "The lead ministry has no abbreviation yet. Ask an administrator to add one, then approve again." | Ask a Core administrator to add the ministry's abbreviation, then approve. |
| "That number is already in use — try again." | Two releases were approved at the same moment. Approve again. |
| "The publish time is more than 5 minutes in the past." | Choose a later time. |
| "A live release's correction goes out immediately — choose Publish now." | A failed correction of a published release can't be scheduled, so **Schedule** isn't offered for it. If you see this, reload the page and choose **Publish now**. |

  2. Check the list. Choose Publish now.

The status shows Publishing..., then Published, usually within a minute. The page updates by itself: "This page updates on its own until the release is done — no need to reload."

Schedule

  1. Choose Schedule. If the release has a planned publish date still ahead, the date and time are filled in from it.
  2. Enter the Date and Time (BC time). A time that has passed shows "Choose a time in the future, or use Publish now."
  3. Choose Confirm schedule. A box asks, for example, "Schedule this release for Friday, November 20, 2026 at 10:00 AM Pacific time?" and lists who will be emailed, as for Publish now.
  4. Choose Schedule.

The release moves to Scheduled. At that time it publishes by itself and the emails go out. Until then nothing is public: not the page, not its files, not the emails.

You can still change a scheduled release. What goes out is the release as saved at the publish time.

Planned publish date (not yet committed), in Publish settings, is only a plan: nothing happens at that time. It shows on Forecast and makes the status Planned. Choose Clear planned date to remove it. Only Schedule commits a time.

Set this in Publish settings before you publish.

  • Send to News On Demand subscribers: ticked for releases, unticked for stories and factsheets, and not available for advisories.

Message What it means
"Set a URL key in Page details before this can be published." A story or factsheet needs a URL key.
"The lead ministry has no abbreviation yet. Ask an administrator to add one, then approve again." Ask a Core administrator to add the ministry's abbreviation, then approve.
"That number is already in use — try again." Two releases were approved at the same moment. Approve again.
"The publish time is more than 5 minutes in the past." Choose a later time.
"A live release's correction goes out immediately — choose Publish now." A failed correction of a published release can't be scheduled, so Schedule isn't offered for it. If you see this, reload the page and choose Publish now.

pages.title: Who is emailed, and when it goes public
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release editors (NRMS.Editor).

Publishing emails people. Publishing again after an unpublish emails only people who weren't reached the first time. Saving, approving, scheduling, correcting and unpublishing don't email anyone.

## When you publish

| What | Who or where | When |
|---|---|---|
| Public news site | The release's own page, and the home, ministry, sector, theme and tag pages that list it. Not for advisories. | Usually within a couple of minutes of the publish time. |
| News On Demand, as it happens | Active subscribers who chose As it happens and either follow any of the release's ministries, sectors, themes or tags, or subscribe to all news. | Soon after it publishes. |
| News On Demand, daily digest | The same people, if they chose the digest. | The next digest, at 5:00 pm BC time. |
| Media distribution lists | Every member of each list you ticked. They get the full text. | Soon after it publishes. |
| The Calendar | The linked activity shows the new status. | Within a minute. |

Subscribers are emailed only if **Send to News On Demand subscribers** is ticked. If nobody follows the release's ministries, sectors, themes or tags, it publishes normally and no subscriber email is sent.

A reporter on a media list you ticked who also gets As-it-happens emails gets one email, the media version. If they chose the daily digest, the release is also in their digest.

Subscriber emails show the release's **Summary** from **Page details**, not its subheadline. Replies to a release email go to the news office's reply address.

Advisories are never sent to subscribers or put on the public site. They go only to their media lists, and once sent they can't be taken back.

## When you correct a published release

Saving any change republishes it at once, with no box asking first. The status shows **Republishing...**, then **Published**.

- The public page shows the change within a couple of minutes.
- Nobody is emailed again. People already emailed keep the first version; the 5 pm digest carries the corrected one if you correct it before 5 pm.
- Media lists can't be changed on a release or factsheet once it has gone out.

## When you unpublish

- The release's page and its files come off the public site, and it leaves the lists on other pages.
- It leaves any Top or Feature spot it held.
- Emails not yet sent are stopped, and it stays out of later digests. Emails already sent can't be recalled.
- It goes back to **Drafts** as approved, with the same numbers and web address. Its status shows **Planned**, because it keeps its old publish time as a plan.

## When you publish it again after an unpublish

The release goes back on the public site at the same address. People who already got it aren't emailed again.

If you unpublished it before all its emails had gone out, the media list members and As-it-happens subscribers it hadn't reached are emailed when you publish it again. Daily-digest subscribers get it only if it is back on the site before the 5 pm digest that would have carried it: 5 pm on the day it first went out, or the next day if it first went out after 5 pm.

The **Publish now** box says so, with the date. Once that 5 pm has passed, it says "That time has passed, so daily digest subscribers who didn't get it then won't."

## Embargoes

There is no separate embargo setting. **Schedule** is the embargo: until the scheduled time, the public page, the files and the emails don't exist outside the Hub. Anyone with Hub access can read the release before then.

pages.title: Correct, feature, unpublish or delete
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release editors (NRMS.Editor).

## Correct a published release

1. Open the release and make the change.
2. Choose **Save changes**.

It republishes at once: no box asks first. The status shows **Republishing...**, then **Published**, usually within a minute. **History** shows "Republished to …"; with **Show all** ticked it also shows "Edited after publishing — will republish". The public page shows the change within a couple of minutes. Nobody is emailed again.

Uploading or removing a file counts as a correction too. If a correction fails, the release shows "This release failed" and stays on the public site as it was. Fix the problem, save, then choose **Publish now**. **Schedule** isn't offered: a failed correction goes out at once.

## Top and Feature spots

Each place on the public site has one Top and one Feature spot: the home page, and each ministry, sector and theme page. A release can take them only while it is published.

1. Open the release. **Top / Feature** says where it is now, such as "Feature on Home", or "Not in a Top or Feature slot anywhere."
2. Choose **Change Top / Feature**. You see **Home** and each ministry, sector and theme the release is filed under, as saved.
3. Switch **Top** or **Feature** on or off for a place.

It changes at once, without **Save changes**, and doesn't republish the release or email anyone. Switching a spot on takes it over from whichever release had it. To see every spot at once, go to **Website** > **What's featured where**.

## Unpublish

Advisories can't be unpublished.

1. Choose **Unpublish**. A box asks "Unpublish this release?"
2. Choose **Confirm unpublish**.

The status shows **Unpublishing...**, then the release goes back to **Drafts**, usually within a minute. Its page and files come off the public site, it leaves any Top or Feature spot, and emails not yet sent are stopped. See [Who is emailed, and when it goes public](manual:editor-what-happens-next).

To put it back, choose **Publish now** or **Schedule**. It keeps its numbers and its web address.

## Delete

You can delete a draft, an approved release or a failed one. A published release, including one whose correction failed, must be unpublished first; until then it has no **Delete**.

1. Choose **Delete**. A box asks "Delete this release?"
2. Choose **Confirm delete**. You are taken to **Drafts**.

- A draft that was never approved is deleted for good: "This draft has never been approved — deleting it is permanent and can't be undone."
- A release with a reference number disappears from the folders and **Search**, but its record is kept: "This release has a reference number (NEWS-00010) — deleting it hides it from the lists but keeps the record."

pages.title: Find a release
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release editors (NRMS.Editor).

## Open a release you know

1. Type into **Find a release**, at the top of the side menu, one of:
   - its reference number, such as NEWS-00007, or just 00007;
   - its release number or URL key, such as 2026HLTH0003-000008;
   - its public web address.
2. Choose **Find**.

The release opens. If nothing has that number, you get **Search** results for what you typed instead.

On screens without their own search or filter box, Ctrl+K (Command+K on a Mac) takes you to **Find a release**.

## Search

1. Choose **Search** in the side menu.
2. Type part of the headline, exactly as it appears, in **Search**.
3. To narrow it, choose a **Ministry** or **Sector**. On its own, without words in **Search**, this does nothing.
4. Choose **Search**.

Typing a reference number, release number or web address here opens the release directly, as **Find a release** does.

Before you search, **Search** lists the five most recently published releases.

Results include drafts, scheduled and published releases, newest first, 20 to a page. Deleted releases don't appear. If nothing matches, you see "No releases match" and your words; if a ministry or sector is chosen, choose **Clear ministry and sector filters** to try again without them.

Search looks at headlines only. To find a release by other words, use **Similar published releases** on a release, or the public site's own search.

To find the releases linked to a Calendar activity, search for its reference with a ministry prefix, such as HLTH-123. If no release is linked to it, or you can't see that activity in the Calendar, you also get the releases with those words in the headline, so COVID-19 finds headlines that mention COVID-19.

pages.title: What's featured where and the Website log
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release editors (NRMS.Editor).

On **Website** you see two tabs. Both only show information.

## What's featured where

The table lists each place on the public site that has a Top or Feature release: **Home**, and each ministry, sector or theme page. **Top** and **Feature** show the release's headline. A dash means the spot is empty. If nothing is set anywhere, the tab says "Nothing is currently Top or Feature anywhere."

Choose a headline to open the release. You set Top and Feature on the release itself; see [Correct, feature, unpublish or delete](manual:editor-correct-unpublish-delete).

## Website log

**Website log** lists every change to the public site's content, newest first: **When**, **Who**, **Area** and **What**. It shows the latest 200 entries. Your Top and Feature changes appear under **Features**, such as "Set as Top for Home".

To see one kind of change, choose it in **Filter by area**. Choose **(all)** to see everything again.

The other areas, such as **Carousel** and **Site settings**, are changed by site editors.

pages.markdown:

## Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Command instead of Ctrl. The shortcuts work from inside text boxes too.

| Keys | What it does |
|---|---|
| Ctrl+S | On a release, saves every part you changed, the same as **Save changes**. |
| Ctrl+Enter | On **New release**, the same as **Create release**. |
| Ctrl+K | Goes to the search or filter box: **Type** on the folders, the **Search** box on **Search**, and **Find a release** everywhere else. |
| Esc | Closes a box or an open panel. |

- **How do I…**: short answers for common tasks.
- **Keyboard shortcuts**: the full list.
- **Glossary**: what terms such as **Planned publish date** and **Media distribution lists** mean.

pages.title: Releases viewer manual
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release viewers (NRMS.Viewer).

You can open every news release, story, factsheet and advisory in the Hub: drafts, scheduled releases and published ones. You can't change them. If something needs changing, ask a release editor.

## What you can do

| Where | What you do there | Help page |
|---|---|---|
| **Releases** | See the drafts, scheduled and published releases, and what is coming up on **Forecast**. | [The release folders](manual:viewer-release-folders) |
| The release itself | Read its text, details and files, open its PDF or public page, and email yourself a copy. | [Read a release](manual:viewer-read-a-release) |
| **Find a release** and **Search** | Open a release by its number, or find it by its headline. | [Find a release](manual:viewer-find-a-release) |
| **Website** | See which releases are featured on the public site, and every change made to the site. | [What's featured where and the Website log](manual:viewer-featured-and-log) |

Release editors also see **New release**, **Actions** and **Similar published releases**. You don't. They have their own manual, the Releases editor manual.

## What you see in the side menu

At the top is **Find a release**. Under **Work** you see **Releases**, **Search** and **Website**.

You may also see **Subscribers** or **Calendar** if you have a role there. Those have their own manuals.

## Signing in

Choose **Sign in with Microsoft** and use your government Microsoft account. You need a Hub account first: if you see "Your account hasn't been set up. Contact an administrator.", ask a Core administrator to add you. Signing out of the Hub doesn't sign you out of Microsoft.

pages.title: The release folders
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release viewers (NRMS.Viewer).

**Releases** has four tabs. **Releases** in the side menu opens the tab you had open last, or **Drafts**.

| Tab | What it lists | In what order |
|---|---|---|
| **Forecast** | Releases planned or scheduled from now on, and the Calendar activities a release may be planned for. | By time. |
| **Drafts** | Releases not yet scheduled or published: drafts, approved releases and failed ones. | Those planned for today or earlier first, then those with no planned time, then later ones. |
| **Scheduled** | Releases set to publish at a time. | Soonest first. |
| **Published** | Releases on the public site, and advisories that have been sent. | Newest first. |

Each row shows the type, the lead ministry, the status and the date. It also shows the page title if it isn't the same as the type, and the Calendar activity it is linked to. On **Drafts** it shows who changed it last. Choose the headline to open the release.

To see one kind only, choose it in **Type**: **Release**, **Story**, **Factsheet** or **Advisory**. The Hub remembers your choice on every tab. If nothing matches, choose **Show every type**.

Each page shows 25 releases. Use **Previous** and **Next** to move between pages.

## What the status means

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Draft** | Not yet approved. |
| **Approved** | Approved and given a reference number, but not yet published or scheduled. |
| **Planned** | It has a planned publish date, but nothing is committed. A planned release that is approved also shows an **Approved** badge. |
| **Scheduled** | It will publish at the time shown. |
| **Publishing...** | Its time has come and it is going out now. |
| **Republishing...** | A correction is going out. |
| **Published** | It is on the public site. An advisory shows **Sent** instead. |
| **Unpublishing...** | It is being taken off the public site. |
| **Failed** | Publishing didn't work. Open it to see why. |

A **Flickr alert** badge means the release went out without its Flickr photo.

## The Forecast

**Forecast** shows what is coming up.

Calendar activities appear only if you have Calendar access, and only the ones you can see in the Calendar. Choose an activity's title to open it in the Calendar. An activity that already has a release planned or scheduled is shown as that release instead. Without Calendar access, the tab says "Calendar activities are listed here for people with Calendar access. Ask a Calendar administrator if you need it."

pages.title: Read a release
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release viewers (NRMS.Viewer).

You see a release just as a release editor does, but you can't change anything and there is nothing to save.

At the top are its type, status, reference number and headline. A draft may also list what is still missing, under "Before this can be approved:" or "Before this can be published:". Those lists are for the release editor.

If you see "This page updates on its own until the release is done — no need to reload.", the release is being published or taken off the site. Its status changes by itself.

On a wide screen, the release is on the left, and **Publish settings** and **Release info** are on the right. On a narrow screen they come one after another.

## The release

- **Documents**: each document's page title, headline, body and contacts. If a document has French text, choose its **French** tab to read it.
- **Page details**: the URL key, location, summary, social media summary and keywords.
- **Categories**: the ministries, sectors, themes and tags it is filed under. Choose **Show categories** to see every choice.
- **Top / Feature**: where the release is a Top or Feature on the public site, such as "Top on Home". Choose **Show Top / Feature** to see every place.
- **Media asset**: the photo or video shown with the release, if it has one.
- **Files**: translations and media files. Choose a file's name to open it.

## Publish settings

**Publish settings** shows the planned publish date, if there is one. It also shows whether the release goes to News On Demand subscribers, and which media distribution lists it is sent to.

## Release info

- **Key** and **Reference (NEWS number)**, or "(none yet)".
- **View on site** opens the public page in a new tab. It works only while the release is published.
- **View PDF** opens the release as a PDF in a new tab.
- **Email me a copy** emails the release to you. You see "Sent to" and your address. The release's **History** records that you did.
- **History** lists what was done and by whom. Tick **Show all** to include every edit.
- **Published copies** lists each time it went out.

If you see "This release doesn't exist, or has been deleted.", it was deleted, or the link you followed is wrong.

## The public news site

**View on site** takes you to the public news site. The site has a page for every ministry, sector, theme and tag, each with its latest 20 posts and an RSS feed. Older news is in the archive, one page per month. Each ministry page also shows its minister, its media contacts, the ministry's website, and its featured topics and services.

The site's **Search** page searches every published post. You can narrow it by **Ministry**, **Sector**, **Content** or **Date**. Each ministry and sector page links to it.

The **Connect** page lists the government's social media accounts and the site's RSS feeds.

pages.title: Find a release
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Release viewers (NRMS.Viewer).

## Open a release you know

1. Type into **Find a release**, at the top of the side menu, one of:
   - its reference number, such as NEWS-00007, or just 00007;
   - its release number or URL key, such as 2026HLTH0003-000008;
   - its public web address.
2. Choose **Find**.

The release opens. If nothing has that number, you get **Search** results for what you typed instead.

## Search

1. Choose **Search** in the side menu.
2. Type part of the headline in **Search**, word for word. Capitals don't matter.
3. To narrow it, choose a **Ministry** or **Sector**. On its own, without words in **Search**, this does nothing.
4. Choose **Search**.

Typing a reference number, release number or web address here opens the release directly, as **Find a release** does.

Before you search, **Search** lists the five most recently published releases.

Results include drafts, scheduled and published releases, newest first, 20 to a page. Deleted releases don't appear. If nothing matches, you see "No releases match" and your words. If a ministry or sector is chosen, choose **Clear ministry and sector filters** to try again without them.

Search looks at headlines only. To find a published release by other words, use the public site's own **Search** page.

To find the releases linked to a Calendar activity, search for its reference with a ministry prefix, such as HLTH-123. If no release is linked to it, or you can't see that activity in the Calendar, you also get the releases with those words in the headline. So COVID-19 finds headlines that mention COVID-19.

pages.title: Subscribers administrator manual
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

You run News On Demand, the service that emails news releases to the public and to reporters. You decide which lists people can subscribe to, you can stop and start all outgoing email, and you watch bounces.

## What only you can do

Subscribers editors and Subscribers viewers can open the same screens, but only you can change these.

| Screen | What it controls | Who notices | Help page |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Subscribers** > **Lists and categories** | Which lists the public can choose, and their order. | People signing up on the public site, and staff adding subscribers. Existing subscribers keep their lists. | [Lists and categories](manual:lists-and-categories) |
| **Subscribers** > **Operations** | Pausing News On Demand sending or all email, the daily bounce summary, which soft bounces count, and the retention purge. | Every subscriber and reporter. A pause holds their email until you resume. | [Operations](manual:subscriber-operations) |

Only you see the **Operations** tab.

## What you share with Subscribers editors

Subscribers editors can do these as well. Subscribers viewers can only look.

| Screen | What you do there | Help page |
|---|---|---|
| **Find subscribers** | Search, change preferences and email addresses, deactivate, delete. | [Find and change subscribers](manual:find-and-change-subscribers) |
| **Add a subscriber** | Sign someone up without a confirmation email. | [Add a subscriber](manual:add-a-subscriber) |

pages.title: Who gets which email
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

Only **Active** subscribers get news email. **Pending**, **Disabled** and **Unsubscribed or deleted** subscribers get none.

## News releases

Each subscriber chooses lists and a timing. Lists are ministries, sectors, themes and tags. **All news** covers every release that names a ministry.

| Timing | What they get |
|---|---|
| **As it happens** | One email for each matching release, soon after it is published. |
| **Daily digest** | One email at 5:00 pm BC time listing the matching releases since the last digest. Media advisories are left out. No matching releases means no digest. |
| **As it happens and daily digest** | Both. |
| **None (media lists only)** | No news release email. This person is here only for media lists. |

A correction to a release never emails anyone again. If a release is unpublished, anything not yet sent is stopped, and it stays out of later digests.

## Emergency alerts

Alerts posted by Emergency Info BC are checked every 5 minutes. A new alert goes at once to everyone active on the **Emergency Info BC Alerts** list, whatever timing they chose. An alert edited later is not sent again.

## Media lists

Release editors choose media lists for a release. Each member of those lists gets the full-text media version. A reporter who is also an **As it happens** subscriber for that release gets one email, the media version, not two.

## Emails about the subscription itself

People who sign up on the public site get an email asking them to confirm. They have no record here until they do. They also get an email when they ask to change their preferences or address. These emails still go out while sending is paused.

Nothing you do on the **Subscribers** screens emails the subscriber. Adding, changing, deactivating and deleting are all silent. Tell the person yourself if they need to know.

pages.title: Find and change subscribers
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

**Find subscribers** lists everyone who has signed up or been added, 50 to a page. From a subscriber's record you change their lists, their address and whether they get email.

## Find someone

1. Type part of their address in **Email contains**.
2. To narrow the list, choose a **Status**.
3. Choose **Search**.
4. Choose an address to open that subscriber's record. **Back to results** on the record returns you to the same results.

The **Status** column shows one of these:

| Status | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Pending** | Never confirmed. They get nothing. Rare; such records are deleted after 10 days when the retention purge is on. |
| **Active** | They get the email they chose. |
| **Disabled** | They get nothing. Staff deactivated them, or their email kept bouncing. Their lists are kept. |
| **Unsubscribed or deleted** | They get nothing. Only they can subscribe again. |

"(needs attention)" after a status means a media list member has a problem to fix on **Media lists**.

## Read a subscriber's record

The record shows **Status**, **Source**, **Registered** and, once they have left, **Ended**.

- **Disabled — after repeated bounces** means bounces disabled them. **Disabled — by staff** means someone deactivated them.
- **Bounced emails counted (last 15 days)** shows how close they are to being disabled. See [Bounces](manual:bounces).
- **Media lists** names the media lists they are on. Change those on **Media lists**.
- **History** lists every change: when, what, who, and details. Adding a **Disabled** record to a media list also shows "Added to a media list while Disabled. News release email stays off". "Subscriber" means the person did it themselves. "Bounce processing" and "Media Hub sync" are automatic. The most recent 500 entries are shown.

## Change their lists or timing

1. Open their record. **Preferences** shows for **Active** and **Disabled** subscribers.
2. Tick **As it happens**, **Daily digest**, or both.
3. Under **Lists**, tick **All news**, or tick the lists they want. Lists they have that are no longer offered show under **No longer offered**. They keep those unless you untick them.
4. Choose **Save preferences**. You see "Preferences saved."

The change applies to the next email. Nobody is emailed about it.

## Change their email address

1. Open their record.
2. Enter the address in **New email** and again in **Confirm new email**.
3. Choose **Change email**. You see "Email address changed. No confirmation email was sent." and the new address shows at the top of the record.

No confirmation email is sent. Links in emails already sent to the old address stop working, except the unsubscribe links.

If the new address once unsubscribed from a media list this person is on, the Hub asks "That address unsubscribed". Choose **Change anyway** only if they have asked to get media releases there again. It counts as adding them back to those lists.

For a Media Hub contact, the record says "This address is managed in Media Hub. Change it there." The address can't be changed here.

## Deactivate or activate someone

1. Open their record.
2. Choose **Deactivate**. The Hub asks "Deactivate this subscriber?" and explains "They receive nothing until activated again. Their lists, including media lists, are kept."
3. Choose **Confirm deactivate**. Their status becomes **Disabled — by staff**.

To bring back a **Disabled** subscriber, choose **Activate**. It happens at once, without a question. You see "Activated. Their bounce count starts again."

## Delete someone

Delete when a person asks to stop all email, or when an address must be removed.

1. Open their record.
2. Choose **Delete**. The Hub asks "Delete this subscriber?" and explains "They stop receiving email and are removed from every media list. Only they can subscribe again."
3. Choose **Confirm delete**.

What this does:

- Their status becomes **Unsubscribed or deleted** at once. Staff can't undo it, and **Add a subscriber** refuses their address while the record exists.
- They are taken off every media list. Adding them to a media list again later doesn't ask about an unsubscribe.
- The record, with their address and history, stays until the retention purge removes it. When the purge is on, it permanently deletes these records 90 days after they ended. See [Operations](manual:subscriber-operations).
- Nobody is emailed.

A **Pending** subscriber's record has only **Delete**.

## Change several at once

1. Search for the subscribers.
2. Tick the box beside each one. The box in the heading row ticks the whole page.
3. Choose **Activate selected**, **Deactivate selected** or **Delete selected**. The button shows how many you ticked.
4. Read the question, then choose **Confirm activate**, **Confirm deactivate** or **Confirm delete**.

Only the ticked rows on the page you are looking at are changed. A message such as "1 changed. 1 skipped: already in that state." tells you the result. Rows are skipped when they are already in that state, or when their status doesn't allow it, such as activating someone who unsubscribed.

## Can't do this?

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| "The two email addresses don't match." | Type the same address in both boxes. |
| "Another subscriber record already has that address." | Choose **Open that record** to see it. Two records can't share an address. |
| "This address is managed in Media Hub. Change it there." | Update the contact in Media Hub. The nightly Media Hub sync brings the change here. |
| "Choose As It Happens, Daily Digest, or both." | A subscriber with lists needs a timing. |
| "Choose at least one list, or all news." | Tick a list or **All news**. Only someone on a media list can have no lists here. |
| "This subscriber's status changed; reload." | Someone else changed them. Reload the page. |
| "Subscriber not found." | The record was removed by the retention purge, or the address in your browser is wrong. |

pages.title: Add a subscriber
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

**Add a subscriber** signs someone up for news release email on their behalf. Add only people who have asked to receive it.

## Add someone

1. Enter their address in **Email** and again in **Confirm email**.
2. Under **Lists**, tick **All news**, or tick the lists they want.
3. Tick **As it happens**, **Daily digest**, or both. **As it happens** starts ticked.
4. Choose **Add subscriber**. Their new record opens.

## What happens next

- They are **Active** straight away. No confirmation email is sent, and they are not told they were added.
- They get the next release that matches their lists. See [Who gets which email](manual:who-gets-which-email).
- Their record shows **Source** "Added by staff", and **History** shows "Added by staff" with your name.

To put a reporter on a media list, use **Media lists** instead. See [Media lists](manual:subscriber-media-lists).

## Can't do this?

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| "The two email addresses don't match." | Type the same address in both boxes. |
| "Choose at least one list, or all news." | Tick a list or **All news**. |
| "Choose As It Happens, Daily Digest, or both." | Tick at least one timing. |
| "That address already has a subscriber record." | Choose **Open their record**. If they are **Disabled**, activate them there. If they unsubscribed or were deleted, only they can sign up again, on the public site. |
| "Couldn't load the list of lists. “All news” still works." | The lists didn't load. Reload the page, or add them to **All news**. |

pages.title: Lists and categories
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

**Lists and categories** decides which lists people can choose when they subscribe, and the order they see them in. Each list shows how many active subscribers it has.

The categories are **Ministries**, **Sectors**, **Themes**, **Tags**, **Emergency Info BC** and **Media distribution lists**. List names come from elsewhere and can't be changed here:

- Ministry, sector, theme and tag names are set by Core administrators.
- Media list names, order and status are set by Core administrators on **Media list names**. Under **Media distribution lists** the screen says "Media lists aren't changed here. Core administrators set these on Media list names."

The **Offered** column shows whether people can choose each list:

| Offered | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Yes** | People can choose it. |
| **No** | You stopped offering it. |
| **No (retired)** | The list was retired where its name is set, such as a ministry that no longer exists. |
| **No (category not offered)** | You stopped offering its whole category. |
| **No (media list)** | A media list. People never choose media lists themselves. |

## Stop offering a list or a category

1. Untick **Offer** and the list's name, such as **Offer Seniors**, on its row. To stop a whole category, untick **Offer** and the category's name under its heading.
2. "Saved" appears beside the box. There is no question first.

The list disappears from the public subscribe page and from the staff **Lists** choices. People who already have it keep it, and still get its releases.

To offer it again, tick the box again.

## Change the order

- Changes apply at once.
- Nobody's subscription is removed, and nobody is emailed.

## Can't do this?

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| "The lists changed while you were looking. They've been reloaded; try again." | Someone else changed the order, or a list was added. Try the move again. |
| "Media lists aren't changed here. Core administrators set these on Media list names." | Media lists can't be offered or reordered here. |
| "Not saved: Couldn't save. Try again." | The change didn't save. Try again. |

pages.title: Media lists
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

**Media lists** holds the reporters on each media list. Release editors pick these lists on a release, and every member gets the full-text media version.

The table shows each list's **Members**, how many **Need attention**, and its **Status**. A **Retired** list can no longer be put on a release. Core administrators add, rename and retire lists on **Media list names**.

Choose a list's name to open it.

## Add a reporter from Media Hub

1. Open the list.
2. Under **Add from Media Hub**, type a name, email or outlet in **Name, email or outlet**.
3. Choose **Search Media Hub**. Each contact shows their addresses, with the preferred one marked.
4. Choose **Add** and the address you want. You see "Added to the list."

## Add an address by hand

Use this for people who aren't in Media Hub.

1. Open the list.
2. Under **Add an address by hand**, enter the **Email address**.
3. Choose **Add to list**. You see "Added to the list."

## What adding does

- The reporter is not emailed. They get the next release sent to this list.
- A new address gets a record that receives media email only.
- An address that is already **Active** keeps its news release email as it was.
- If the address already has a record that is **Disabled** or **Unsubscribed or deleted**, adding makes it **Active** again, for media email only. **As it happens**, **Daily digest** and their news lists are switched off. Media lists they were already on are kept.
- For a **Disabled** person, their bounce count starts again, and **History** shows "Added to a media list while Disabled. News release email stays off", with what was switched off under **Detail**.
- When the address was **Disabled**, you see "Added to the list. Their news release email stays off; open their record to turn it on." instead of "Added to the list."
- If a **Disabled** person also wants news release email again, choose **open their record** in that message. Tick **As it happens** or **Daily digest** and their lists, then choose **Save preferences**.
- If the person left this list by unsubscribing, the Hub asks "This person unsubscribed" and says when. Choose **Add anyway** only if they have asked to get media releases again.

## Remove a reporter

1. Open the list.
2. Choose **Remove** and their address on their row. The Hub asks "Remove [their address] from this list?" and explains "If this is their last list and they were added only for media lists, they stop receiving email altogether."
3. Choose **Confirm remove**. You see "Removed from the list."

Nobody is emailed. If it was their last list and they were added only for media lists, their status becomes **Unsubscribed or deleted**. You can add them back later without the unsubscribe question.

## Fix a member who needs attention

A flagged member shows the reason under **Needs attention**:

| Reason | What happened |
|---|---|
| **Bouncing** | Their last 10 emails in 15 days all bounced. They are still on the list and still sent email. |
| **Media Hub email removed** | The address they use was removed from their Media Hub contact. |
| **Media Hub email belongs to another subscriber** | Media Hub moved them to an address another record already has. |
| **Media Hub email isn't valid** | Media Hub has an address that isn't a real email address. |
| **Media Hub email opted out of a media list this member is on** | Media Hub moved them to an address that unsubscribed from one of their lists, so they were kept at their old address. |

To fix a bouncing member:

1. Check with Media Relations that their mailbox works again.
2. Choose **Resolve** and their address. The Hub asks "Clear the bouncing flag?"
3. Choose **Clear flag**. You see "Resolved. Their bounce count starts again."

To fix a Media Hub problem:

1. Choose **Resolve** and their address. **Resolve this member** shows their Media Hub addresses.
2. Choose the address to use, then **Use this email**. You see "Email updated and flag cleared."
3. Or choose **Clear the flag only** to keep their current address. For an opted-out address, the next Media Hub sync flags them again. Update the contact in Media Hub instead, or remove them and add them again.

## Left this list by unsubscribing

This section lists people who unsubscribed from this list themselves, with when they left and whether they are **Back on the list**. The most recent 200 are shown.

## Media Hub sync

Every night, News On Demand picks up changed Media Hub contacts. **Media Hub sync** shows when it last ran and what it changed.

To run it now, choose **Sync with Media Hub now**. You see "Sync finished." and its counts. A long sync may stop part-way and carry on at the next scheduled run.

## Can't do this?

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| "That isn't a valid email address." | Check the address. |
| "Media Hub isn't responding. Try again, or add the address by hand." | Media Hub is down. |
| "Media Hub isn't set up on this site. Add the address by hand instead." | This site has no Media Hub connection. |
| "That contact or email is no longer in Media Hub." | Search Media Hub again. |
| "A sync is already running. Try again in a few minutes." | Wait for the running sync to finish. |
| "That address belongs to another subscriber. Choose another email, or remove this member." | Pick a different address. |
| "This member changed while you were looking. Close this, and try again." | Someone else changed them. Close the box and try again. |
| "Couldn't remove. Try again." | The removal didn't save. |

pages.title: Reports
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

**Reports** shows who receives what, who left, and what was sent. Dates and times are BC time.

| Report | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Active subscribers by list** | How many active subscribers each list has now, split by timing. **Show members** lists the people on one list. |
| **Recent unsubscribes** | Everyone who unsubscribed, or was deleted by staff, in the last 90 days. |
| **Sends per release** | For each release or alert published in the dates you choose, the as-it-happens and media list emails. |
| **Daily digest runs** | Each 5:00 pm digest: how many subscribers and emails. |
| **Distribution sent and bounced** | Every email sent from any app, by day and sender. |

## Choose dates

**Sends per release**, **Daily digest runs** and **Distribution sent and bounced** cover the last 30 days at first.

1. Enter **From (BC date)** and **To (BC date)**. Up to 92 days at a time.
2. Choose **Show**.

## Download a CSV

Each report has a **Download** link for a CSV file that opens in Excel.

These downloads contain email addresses:

- **Download members (CSV)** on **Active subscribers by list**, after you choose **Show members**.
- **Download list with addresses (CSV)** on **Recent unsubscribes**.

Each address download is recorded with your name and the report, never the addresses. Keep the file only as long as you need it. Subscribers viewers can't download addresses.

## Read the numbers

- **Handed off, not bounced** counts emails handed to Distribution, the sending service, less bounces. It is not proof of delivery. An email still queued, or one Distribution failed to send, still counts.
- **Not sent** means not yet handed off, including a send still going out.
- **Items in window** on **Daily digest runs** is worked out when you open the report. A release withdrawn since the run no longer counts, so an older run's number can go down.
- **Distribution sent and bounced** won't match the other two reports. It counts by the day it sent, has its own **Failed** column, and counts every bounce. The other reports go by the day the release was published or the digest ran, and count only bounces matched to a news email.
- **Recent unsubscribes** doesn't list people disabled by bounces. Find them on **Find subscribers** with the **Disabled** status. It does include people who unsubscribed in the old News On Demand, at the dates they left.

## Can't do this?

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| "Choose a range of 92 days or fewer." | Shorten the dates. |
| "The start date must be on or before the end date." | Swap the dates. |
| "Enter real dates." | Check both dates. |
| "That list doesn't exist any more." | The list was removed. Go back to the report. |
| "Distribution is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes." | Only **Distribution sent and bounced** is affected. The other reports still work. |

pages.title: Operations
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

**Operations** stops and starts outgoing email, sets who gets the daily bounce summary, and controls the retention purge. Only Subscribers administrators see it.

## Pause News On Demand sending

Pause this to hold news email, for example during an election period or while a problem is fixed.

1. Under **News On Demand sending**, choose **Pause News On Demand sending**. The Hub asks "Pause News On Demand sending?" and explains "News On Demand keeps recording releases and building emails but holds them until you resume. Nothing is dropped." and says who is emailed about it.
2. Choose **Confirm pause**. You see "News On Demand sending paused." and the section shows **Paused**.

While paused, no as-it-happens, digest, emergency alert or media list email leaves News On Demand. Confirmation emails to people signing up still go out.

To resume, choose **Resume News On Demand sending**, then **Confirm resume**. The Hub warns that held emails start going out straight away.

## Pause Distribution

Distribution is the service that sends email for every app. Pause it only when email from all of them must stop.

1. Under **Distribution**, choose **Pause Distribution**. The Hub asks "Pause Distribution?" and explains "No email goes out from any app, except system notices, until you resume. Queued email is kept." and says who is emailed about it.
2. Choose **Confirm pause**. You see "Distribution paused."

System notices still go out while paused. These include sign-up confirmations, manage-subscription links, the bounce summary and the pause emails themselves.

To resume, choose **Resume Distribution**, then **Confirm resume**. The Hub warns that queued email starts going out straight away.

## Before you resume after a long pause

Everything held goes out when you resume, however old it is. After a long pause, decide first whether old releases should still be sent. An email held more than 24 hours that then fails to send is not tried again.

## Who is told

Each pause and resume emails the operations inbox with your name and the time, and the question says "The operations inbox is emailed." If this site has no operations inbox, nobody is emailed, and the question says "No one is emailed about it." Subscribers are never told.

## Bounce summary

The bounce summary is a daily email at 8:00 am listing bounced subscribers. It is sent only when there were bounces. See [Bounces](manual:bounces) for what it contains.

The section shows where it goes now:

- "Using the server default:" followed by an address means no one has chosen an address here, so the site's own address is used. The box is empty on purpose.
- "No address is set, so no summary is sent." means nobody gets it.

To send it somewhere else:

1. Enter the address in **Bounce summary email**.
2. Choose **Save address**. You see "Bounce summary address saved."

To go back to the site's own address, choose **Use the server default**. You see "Using the server default again." Saving the box empty does the same.

## Soft bounces counted as hard

A soft bounce is a temporary failure, such as a full mailbox. Its code starts with 4. Soft bounces never count toward disabling a subscriber, except the codes you list here. Those count like a hard bounce from the next bounce on, never for earlier ones.

1. Enter codes in **Soft codes counted as hard**, such as 4.2.2, separated by commas.
2. Choose **Save codes**. You see "Soft bounce codes saved."

Leave the box empty to count none.

## Emergency alerts feed

This section shows when the Emergency Info BC feed was last checked and how many alerts were new. Nothing here can be changed. A warning means the last check failed; it tries again every 5 minutes by itself.

The first time a feed is read, its alerts are recorded without emailing anyone. Only alerts posted after that are sent.

## Retention purge

The retention purge permanently deletes old personal information. Leave it **Off** until the business has set retention rules.

When on, every night at 3:00 am it deletes:

- sign-ups that were never confirmed, after 10 days;
- people who unsubscribed or were deleted more than 90 days ago, with their history and delivery records.

It never deletes subscribers disabled by bounces. When it deletes someone who had left a media list by unsubscribing, it keeps that they left the list, without their address, so adding that address back still asks first.

**If it ran now, it would delete** shows the counts before you turn it on. While it is on, the section also shows how its last run went. While it is off, no last run is shown.

1. Choose **Turn on the retention purge**. The Hub asks "Turn on the retention purge?" and says how many subscribers and links the next run deletes "for good, and keeps doing so every night. This can't be undone."
2. Choose **Turn on purge**. You see "Retention purge turned on."

Deleted records can't be brought back. To stop it, choose **Turn off the retention purge**, then **Turn off purge**. Nothing more is deleted.

Links in sent emails are cleared every night 10 days after they expire, whether the purge is on or off. They stopped working long before.

Records imported from the old system that had already ended are kept until 90 days after the import.

## Test bounce upload

This section shows on test sites only, where every email is redirected and real bounces never arrive.

Links in sent emails are cleared every night 10 days after they expire, whether the purge is on or off. They stopped working long before.

Records imported from the old system that had already ended are kept until 90 days after the import.

This section shows on test sites only, where every email is redirected and real bounces never arrive.

  2. Choose Upload bounce. You see "Uploaded. Bounce processing picks it up within 15 minutes."

pages.title: Bounces
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Subscribers administrators (NoD.Admin).

A bounce is an email that comes back undelivered. A hard bounce means the address doesn't work, such as a mailbox that no longer exists. A soft bounce is temporary, such as a full mailbox.

## When a subscriber is disabled

When a subscriber's last 10 emails within 15 days have all hard-bounced, News On Demand acts on its own:

- A subscriber who is not on any media list is disabled. Their status becomes **Disabled — after repeated bounces**, and they get nothing more. Their record and lists are kept. The retention purge never deletes them.
- A media list member is never disabled. They are flagged **Bouncing** on **Media lists** and keep being sent media and news release email. Tell Media Relations.

A daily digest counts as one email, however many releases it lists. Soft bounces don't count, unless their code is listed under **Soft bounces counted as hard** on [Operations](manual:subscriber-operations).

A subscriber's record shows **Bounced emails counted (last 15 days)** once any have bounced.

## Bring a bounced subscriber back

- They can sign up again on the public site. The confirmation email reaching them proves the mailbox works.
- Or, once you know the mailbox works, open their record and choose **Activate**. Their bounce count starts again.

For a bouncing media list member, choose **Resolve** on the list. See [Media lists](manual:subscriber-media-lists).

## The daily bounce summary

The summary is emailed at 8:00 am to the address set on **Operations**, with the subject "News On Demand - Bounce Manager" and the date. It is sent only when something bounced since the last one.

It has these parts:

| Part | What to do |
|---|---|
| Bounce reports processed | The totals, including auto-replies and other messages that weren't bounces. |
| **Hard bounces**: count toward 10 in 15 days | One line per bounce: the address, the code and the outcome, such as recorded, disabled or flagged. |
| **Soft bounces**: not counted, usually no action needed | Usually nothing to do. |
| **Unrecorded bounces**: not counted; check the bounce mailbox | Bounces that matched no news email, such as a bounced sign-up confirmation. If an address keeps appearing and the line says "NoD subscriber", find and delete that subscriber. |

A line in bold is a media list member. Tell Media Relations each time one appears, even if they are already flagged. The soft and unrecorded parts stop at 500 lines each and say how many more there were; the rest are in the bounce mailbox.

pages.title: Calendar administrator manual
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Calendar administrators (Calendar.Administrator) and Calendar system administrators (Calendar.SysAdmin).

You run the Corporate Calendar: who can use it, the choices offered on activities, and which comm contact looks after each activity. If you belong to an HQ organization, you also review what the ministries enter.

## Which administrator you are

Your role, and whether one of your ministries is an HQ organization such as GCPE Headquarters, decide what you can do.

- **Administrator**: you manage Calendar users and their access. You transfer and delete activities of your own ministries.
- **HQ Administrator**: an Administrator or system administrator whose ministries include an HQ organization. You see every ministry's activities, deleted ones included. You review activities, and you can transfer and delete activities of any ministry.
- **System Administrator**: everything an Administrator can do, plus every lookup, the **Undelivered events** tab, and giving the **System Administrator** role. You can also change the access of HQ staff.

## What only you can do

Calendar advanced users, editors and read-only users can't do any of this.

| Where | What you do there | Who can | Help page |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Calendar access** | Give or change a person's Calendar role and ministries. | Every administrator, with limits. | [Calendar access](manual:calendar-admin-access) |
| **Calendar** > **Users** | Keep contact details and comm-contact ranks. Deactivate, reactivate or link people who use only the Calendar. | Every administrator. | [Calendar users](manual:calendar-users) |
| **Calendar** > **Transfer** | Move every activity of one comm contact to another. | Every administrator. HQ Administrators across ministries. | [Transfer activities](manual:calendar-transfer) |
| **Calendar** > **Lookups** | The choices offered on activities, such as HQ tags and event planners. | Administrators change 4 lookups. System administrators change all 11. | [Calendar lookups](manual:calendar-lookups) |
| **Delete** on an activity | Delete an activity. | Every administrator. | [Delete an activity](manual:calendar-delete-activity) |
| The activity list | **Review selected**, deleted activities and the **Exec Look Ahead** report. | HQ Administrators. | [HQ review](manual:calendar-hq-review) |
| **Calendar** > **Undelivered events** | Send again activity changes that Releases refused. | System administrators. | [Undelivered events](manual:calendar-undelivered-events) |

## What you share with other Calendar users

Everyone with Calendar access uses the list, filters, **My Queries**, **Updates**, **Excel export** and the **Look Ahead**, **30/60/90** and **Planning** reports. Editors and above create, change and clone their ministries' activities. HQ staff at Advanced and above also have **Corporate Queries**, the **Look Ahead filter** and **Review**.

The [Calendar advanced user manual](manual:calendar-advanced), the [Calendar editor manual](manual:calendar-editor) and the [Calendar read-only manual](manual:calendar-readonly) cover that work.

## Where your changes show up

- Role, ministry and account changes reach the Calendar within a minute.
- Activity changes reach **Releases** within a minute. Release editors who also have Calendar access see confirmed activities with an "Approved" category on the **Forecast** tab, and can plan a release from them. Confidential and deleted activities never appear there.
- Nothing in this manual emails anyone.

## What you see in the side menu

Under **Work** you see **Calendar**. Under **Administration** you see **Calendar access**.

The Calendar's tabs are **Calendar**, **Updates**, **Lookups**, **Users** and **Transfer**. System administrators also see **Undelivered events**.

pages.title: Calendar access
pages.markdown:
**Who this is for:** Calendar administrators (Calendar.Administrator) and Calendar system administrators (Calendar.SysAdmin).

**Calendar access**, under **Administration** in the side menu, gives a person a Calendar role and the ministries they work for. Each person has one role or **No Calendar access**.

The table shows everyone with a Hub account: **Name**, **Email**, **Calendar role** and **Ministries**. Inactive people are hidden until you tick **Show inactive users, including those with no email**.

## What you can give

- The roles, lowest to highest, are **Read Only**, **Editor**, **Advanced**, **Administrator** and **System Administrator**.
- Administrators can give any role up to **Administrator**. Only system administrators can give **System Administrator**.
- You can give any ministry, not just your own.
- HQ organizations are marked "— HQ" in the ministry list. Their members see every ministry in the Calendar. Only HQ Administrators and system administrators are offered them.
- HQ Administrator isn't a separate role: give **Administrator** and tick an HQ ministry.

## Give or change someone's access

The person needs a Hub account first. Only a Core administrator can add one.

1. Type part of their name or email in **Find a user by name or email**.
2. Choose **Edit** on their row.
3. Choose their **Calendar role**.
4. Under **Ministries**, tick every ministry they work for. A role needs at least one ministry.
5. Choose **Save Calendar access**. You see "Saved Calendar access for" followed by their name.

Saving replaces the person's whole ministry list with what is ticked.

You can make the same change from the person's page on **Calendar** > **Users**: choose **Edit Calendar access for** followed by their name.

## Remove someone's access

1. Choose **Edit** on their row.
2. Choose **No Calendar access** in **Calendar role**.
3. Choose **Save Calendar access**.

Their activities keep them as comm contact. To hand those activities to someone else, use [Transfer activities](manual:calendar-transfer).

## What happens next

- The change reaches the Calendar within a minute.
- A person whose access was removed sees "You don't have Calendar access. Ask a Calendar administrator." on their next click in the Calendar. They stay signed in to the Hub.
- Release editors see Calendar activities on the **Forecast** only if they have Calendar access, and only the activities that access lets them see.
- Nobody is emailed.

## When Edit isn't offered

Some rows show a note instead of **Edit**.

| Note | What it means |
|---|---|
| "You can't change your own Calendar access." | Ask another administrator or a Core administrator. |
| "Only a System Administrator or a Core administrator can change this user's access." | The person is a system administrator and you are an Administrator. |
| "Only an HQ Administrator, a System Administrator or a Core administrator can change this user's access." | The person belongs to an HQ organization and you don't. |
| "Only a Core administrator can give Calendar access to an inactive user who has none." | The person's Hub account is inactive and has no Calendar role. Ask a Core administrator. |

If you have no ministry yourself, the Calendar shows "You aren't in any ministry yet, so there are no activities to show you. Ask another Calendar administrator or a Core administrator to add your ministry." You can't add it yourself.

## Can't do this?

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| "choose at least one ministry for a Calendar role" | Tick a ministry, or choose **No Calendar access**. |
| "Health is no longer active or doesn't exist. Untick it, then save again." | The named ministry was deactivated while you were editing. Untick it. A person who already had a deactivated ministry keeps it when you save. |
